questions.q: When Peter and John laid hands on believers in Samaria to receive the Holy Spirit, Simon the Magician saw this and offered them what?
options: His book of magical arts
Money, to buy the power to impart the Holy Spirit
To become a full-time servant of the apostles
Land to build a new church
questions.explain: Simon offered them money, saying, "Give me this power also, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit." (Acts 8:18-19). This incident gave rise to the term 'simony'.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)

questions.q: How did Peter sternly rebuke Simon the Magician for his foolish offer? (Acts 8:20)
options: "May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!"
"You shall be blind and not see the sun for a season."
"Depart from us, for you are a worker of iniquity!"
"You will be cast into the outer darkness!"
questions.explain: Peter rebuked his wicked heart, stating: "May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money! You have neither part nor lot in this matter..." (Acts 8:20-21).

questions.q: In Acts 9:32-35, Peter visited the saints living in Lydda. Whom did he heal there after the man had been bedridden for eight years?
options: Bartimaeus
Lazarus
Aeneas
Jairus
questions.explain: There he found a man named Aeneas, bedridden for eight years, who was paralyzed. Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; rise and make your bed." And immediately he rose.

questions.q: While in Joppa, Peter raised a devoted Christian woman from the dead who was full of good works and acts of charity. What was her name?
options: Lydia
Priscilla
Dorcas (Tabitha)
Phoebe
questions.explain: Now there was in Joppa a disciple named Tabitha, which, translated, means Dorcas. She was full of good works and acts of charity. Peter prayed, and she was raised back to life (Acts 9:36-42).

options: A devout Jewish high priest in Jerusalem
A centurion of the Italian Cohort in Caesarea who feared God
A silversmith in Ephesus who caused a riot
A tax collector from Jericho
questions.explain: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion of what was known as the Italian Cohort, a devout man who feared God with all his household, gave alms generously, and prayed continually.

questions.q: Before Peter went to the house of Cornelius, he had a vision of a great sheet descending from heaven containing all kinds of animals. What was the central lesson God taught Peter through this vision?
options: That Christians should no longer eat meat at all
That God wanted him to become a farmer
That Peter should start a business trading exotic animals
That what God has made clean, Peter must not call common or unclean
questions.explain: The voice said, "What God has made clean, do not call common." This vision was a metaphor teaching Peter that the gospel was for the Gentiles as well, and they should not be considered unclean.

questions.q: When Peter returned to Jerusalem, the "circumcision party" criticized him (Acts 11:1-3). What was their primary accusation against Peter?
options: He had gone to uncircumcised men and eaten with them.
He charged money for healing people in Caesarea.
He refused to pray at the temple.
He allowed women to preach in the synagogue.
questions.explain: They criticized him, saying, "You went to uncircumcised men and ate with them." Strict Jewish tradition forbade such close fellowship with Gentiles.

questions.q: King Herod arrested Peter and imprisoned him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover. How was Peter miraculously released? (Acts 12:6-11)
options: An earthquake shook the prison doors open.
An angel of the Lord woke him, his chains fell off, and they walked past the guards.
The Roman governor ordered his release due to a lack of evidence.
The early church bribed the guards to let him go.
questions.explain: While Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, an angel of the Lord stood next to him, and a light shone. The angel woke him, the chains fell off his hands, and the iron gate opened of its own accord.

questions.q: How did King Herod die shortly after he had accepted the crowd shouting that his voice was "the voice of a god, and not of a man"? (Acts 12:21-23)
options: He was struck by lightning in the palace courtyard.
He was assassinated by his own bodyguards.
He fell from a great height during a public speech.
He was struck down by an angel and eaten by worms because he did not give God the glory.
questions.explain: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give God the glory, and he was eaten by worms and breathed his last.
